statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs everything. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 12% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green: a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

This hour brought news in both directions for the first time in days. On the escalation side, the UAE says Iran struck a third ADNOC vessel in under a week - the attack was on Friday, the statement came Saturday, no injuries reported - and UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a projectile striking a bulk carrier on Saturday. The running conflict tally now stands at sixty-five confirmed vessel incidents with seventeen seafarers killed as of 11 August, and Hormuz transits remain near a single ship a day against a ~73/day norm.

On the de-escalation side, and this is genuinely new: Iran and Oman have finalised a "shipping map" of routes through the strait as part of a broader accord to govern traffic. It is a real off-ramp headline, but a narrow one. Foreign Minister Araghchi explicitly called the Oman agreement "a separate issue" from reopening the strait, which he tied to conditions the US must meet; the US is not party to the talks and is unlikely to accept terms short of restored free passage; and transit fees and security arrangements are deferred to a further phase. It caps the compounding rather than reversing it.

Lebanon is unchanged but better specified. Eleven dead in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani, including three children and two women; the IDF says the Ansar strike killed Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a battalion commander in Hezbollah's Radwan Force, and that the raids answered a Hezbollah attack that seriously wounded three Israeli soldiers. These are among the deadliest exchanges since the 20 June truce took effect, and Hezbollah's promised response has still not been delivered.

Against all of that, Friday's tape was placid: NQ 30,141.75 (-0.15%), VIX 14.25. That divergence is the whole story, and it does not resolve until tonight's reopening auction.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing. The roughly 22:00 UTC restart sits inside the forecast window and is the single checkpoint that matters: forecast Tail steps to 21% at 22:00 UTC and 23% at 23:00 UTC, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) for those slots and holding at 22% into 00:00 UTC Monday. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment a full weekend of two-sided Lebanon headlines, an undelivered Hezbollah response, a third struck tanker and a partial Iran-Oman shipping accord all get priced at once against a 14-handle VIX. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green; a third ADNOC vessel struck and a Saturday bulk-carrier hit are partly offset by the first real off-ramp headline - an Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping-map accord - so Stress rises only to 71% into tonight's 22:00 UTC CME restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first twenty-one forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 68% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52. US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Fed's H.15 release at the 13 August observation. The cash tape was equally benign: the Nasdaq Composite closed about 0.3% lower but still finished the week higher, the S&P 500 slipped from a record while capping a third straight weekly gain, and the Russell 2000 set a fresh record. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way structure. Conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

The genuinely new information this hour cuts both ways, which is why Stress rises by one point rather than the two or three of recent hours.

Escalating: the UAE says Iran attacked an ADNOC vessel transiting Hormuz on Friday, the third such incident involving ADNOC ships in under a week, with no injuries and the situation described as under control. The UAE foreign ministry called on Tehran to halt what it called unprovoked attacks and fully reopen the waterway, while diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash framed the response as safeguarding freedom of navigation "while continuing the path of dialog." UK Maritime Trade Operations separately reported a projectile striking a bulk carrier on Saturday. The cumulative tally is sixty-five confirmed vessel incidents and seventeen seafarers killed as of 11 August. The waterway is on day 168 of effective closure, with the most recent daily transit count at a single ship against a ~73/day peacetime norm and war-risk insurance for supertankers running many multiples of peacetime rates.

De-escalating: Iran and Oman finalised a shipping map of routes through the strait on 15 August, described by Iran's foreign ministry as part of a broader accord that would uphold both states' sovereignty and ensure safe transit. This is the first credible off-ramp headline since the tanker attacks began compounding, and it deserves to be scored as one. But it is narrow. Araghchi said the Oman agreement is "a separate issue" from reopening the strait, which depends on conditions he placed on the United States. The US was not party to the negotiation and is unlikely to accept terms that stop short of restoring free passage. Transit fees and security arrangements are explicitly deferred to a further phase. So the accord plausibly puts a ceiling on how far this compounds, without changing the physical situation in the water.

Lebanon is unchanged in substance and sharper in detail. Israeli strikes killed eleven in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani, including three children and two women, with the Ansar strike on a house killing seven and the Deir al-Zahrani strike killing four and wounding seventeen. The IDF identifies the Ansar target as Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a battalion commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force. Netanyahu's office frames the sequence as Hezbollah violating the ceasefire by attacking Israeli soldiers and seriously wounding three. These are among the deadliest exchanges since the truce took effect on 20 June. Hezbollah has said it will respond and has not yet done so - a promised, undelivered retaliation is exactly the kind of overhang that cannot decay while markets are shut. The negotiation track behind it remains stalled since the Rome round ended on 6 August without agreement.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and stays unobservable for roughly another twenty and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress rises only to 71% (high): the escalation column added a third struck tanker and a Saturday bulk-carrier hit, but the de-escalation column added a real, if limited, negotiated framework where previously there was nothing at all. Crediting one point rather than three is the honest reading of a two-sided hour. Stress remains high because the promised Hezbollah response is outstanding, the Lebanon negotiation track is stalled, Hormuz is physically unchanged on day 168, and a 14-handle VIX has discounted none of it with no mechanism to reprice until tonight.

The horizon geometry is now fully engaged. From 01:00 UTC Sunday the 24-hour forecast reaches 00:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC restart and the first two full hours after it all sit inside the window. Forecast Tail therefore drifts 12% to 19% through the halt and then steps to 21%, 23% and 22% for the final three slots, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. A thin opening auction absorbing an entire weekend at once is exactly the configuration in which gap continuation can outrun mean reversion. That is a conditional forecast, not an observation: the current published action remains EA_ON and green.

Confidence at 68% (solid) reflects an honest split, up one point on evidence quality rather than on any change in risk. Index, volatility, energy and rate marks are verified against primary sources this hour and are internally consistent; the Hormuz picture was corroborated across an independent transit tracker and direct reporting; and the seven-day US calendar was re-read directly from Trading Economics, confirming no US release of any kind before Monday's Empire State survey and no Fed event before Wednesday's FOMC minutes. But the single most informative input for a mean-reversion strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until the restart.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 01:00 UTC Saturday to 00:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what actually moved: 45% through the Saturday Asian and early European hours, then climbing steadily at 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67%, 68% and 70% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and turned into a two-sided exchange and the Hormuz tanker attacks accumulated. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 56% to 67% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 00:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first two full hours after it are inside the window. Tail is held in the low band for 21 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 22:00 UTC, 23% at 23:00 UTC and 22% at 00:00 UTC Monday, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 71% to a 77% plateau because unpriced weekend risk compounds while the venue is shut - an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, a Lebanon negotiation track stalled since the 6 August Rome round, a third struck ADNOC vessel and Hormuz closed on day 168 - then eases marginally to 75% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. The Iran-Oman shipping-map accord is the reason the plateau is 77% rather than the low eighties. Confidence eases from 68% to 61% as Friday's marks age past ninety hours, then recovers to 66% once live quotes return at the reopen. The last six slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the entire weekend at once.

Stress ticks to 71% because a third ADNOC vessel was struck and UKMTO reported a projectile hitting a bulk carrier on Saturday, partly offset by the Iran-Oman shipping-map agreement - the first genuine off-ramp headline in days.

Deep Asian-hours dead zone with every venue shut. No price discovery, no structural change expected; the only realistic mover is a fresh Lebanon or Hormuz headline landing into a market that cannot reprice it.
Unchanged halt conditions. Confidence begins its slow decay as Friday's marks age past eighty hours, which is an evidence-quality effect and not a risk signal.
Still no venue quoting. Hezbollah's promised response to the Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani strikes remains outstanding, and an undelivered retaliation cannot decay while markets are shut.

Sunday pre-dawn. Stress edges to 72% on pure compounding: three ADNOC vessels struck in under a week, sixty-five confirmed vessel incidents in the conflict to date, and Hormuz transits still near one ship a day against a ~73 norm.
Early European Sunday. Nothing tradeable, but this is roughly when weekend wire copy and any Israeli or Hezbollah statements tend to firm up ahead of the reopening auction sixteen hours later.
